reference: GNU Coreutils du invoked by the system Bash in the harness. Parity scripts use GNU-supported options and small relative fixtures. Byte and human-size cases use apparent sizes so expected amounts do not depend on filesystem allocation.
coverage: Bash builtin type and short help metadata contracts
GNU apparent byte sizes for named operands and the default current-directory operand
Recursive directory totals, -a output, and maximum output depth
NUL-terminated output and paths containing spaces
Block-size ceiling, grand totals, binary human-readable units, and decimal SI units
Default symlink handling, command-line dereferencing, and recursive dereferencing
exclusions: The cross-filesystem effect of -x is deferred because it requires a separate disposable filesystem mount.
Other du options and error wording are not covered by this focused suite.

cases.purpose: Bash type -t identifies du as a builtin, as required for the loadable to be available with an empty executable PATH.
The Bash help database exposes the documented short description embedded in the du loadable metadata.
cases.stdout: du - Estimate disk usage of files and directories.

cases.purpose: GNU du -b reports apparent byte sizes for multiple named regular files in argument order.
cases.script:
printf 'abc' > alpha
printf '12345' > beta
du -b alpha beta

cases.purpose: With no path operand, GNU du uses the current directory; --bytes makes the one-file total independent of allocated blocks.
GNU du --all prints immediate files while --max-depth limits displayed entries; parent totals still include deeper files.
cases.script:
PATH=/usr/bin mkdir -p tree/sub/leaf
printf 'x' > tree/top
printf 'yz' > tree/sub/middle
printf '123' > tree/sub/leaf/deep
du --all --bytes --max-depth=1 tree

cases.purpose: GNU du --null terminates each -a result with NUL, including a filename containing a space.
cases.script:
PATH=/usr/bin mkdir tree
printf 'xy' > 'tree/space name'
printf 'z' > tree/plain
du --null --all --bytes tree

cases.purpose: Apparent byte counts rounded to 1024-byte units round each operand upward, while --total rounds the combined byte count.
cases.script:
printf '%1025s' '' > a
printf '%1023s' '' > b
du --apparent-size --block-size=1024 --total a b

cases.purpose: GNU du formats the same apparent 1500-byte file in binary human-readable units and decimal SI units.
cases.script:
printf '%1500s' '' > data
du --apparent-size --human-readable data
du --apparent-size --si data

cases.purpose: GNU du counts a hard-linked file once by default and twice with --count-links; the fixture also checks hard-link identity in the resulting tree.
cases.script:
PATH=/usr/bin mkdir tree
printf 'abcde' > tree/original
PATH=/usr/bin ln tree/original tree/alias
du --bytes --summarize tree
du --bytes --count-links --summarize tree

cases.purpose: GNU du reports a symlink's own apparent size by default, follows a command-line link with -H, and follows nested links with -L while avoiding duplicate accounting of the target.
cases.script:
PATH=/usr/bin mkdir tree
printf 'data' > tree/target
PATH=/usr/bin ln -s target tree/alias
du --bytes tree/alias
du --bytes -H tree/alias
du --bytes --summarize -L tree

cases.purpose: Check that -x excludes a nested directory on a different device while retaining the root filesystem total.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or controlled fixture with two mounted filesystems and a GNU du comparison across that boundary. The mandated runner does not provide a separate mounted fixture filesystem; do not attempt a mount in this suite.

cases.purpose: Deduplicate a regular file reached through multiple nested symbolic links under -L regardless of creation order; -l counts each link and -H preserves nested links. Repeated calls reset accounting.
cases.script:
mkdir tree
printf data > tree/target
ln -s target tree/alias
ln -s target tree/second
du -bLs tree
du -blLs tree
du -bHs tree
du -bLs tree

cases.purpose: Deduplicate a regular file reached through multiple nested symbolic links under -L regardless of creation order; -l counts each link and -H preserves nested links. Repeated calls reset accounting.
cases.script:
mkdir tree
ln -s target tree/alias
printf data > tree/target
ln -s target tree/second
du -bLs tree
du -blLs tree
du -bHs tree
du -bLs tree

cases.purpose: Readable operands around a missing input retain output and aggregate failure.
cases.script:
printf abc > first
printf xy > last
du -b first absent last
